transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Can we check if anyone here feels really strongly about leading the pitch? If not, maybe we just pick whoever has the clearest plan. I don't want us to get stuck.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: I don't mind helping organize, but maybe we should hear if anyone already has a full plan in mind? I can step in if no one else wants to, but happy to support.

transcript.name: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen
transcript.text: Before we move on, has anyone who hasn't spoken yet been thinking about leading? If so, I’d like to hear your thoughts. If not, we can talk about possible plans together.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: I’m not looking to take the lead, but I think what matters most is having a clear plan this time. Maybe we should first outline exactly what we’re pitching, then see who feels best placed to head it up?

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: I'm happy to handle the technical side and double-check our numbers, but if someone else wants to run point on the pitch itself, that's fine by me. If nobody's up for it, I can do it, but I won't be flashy.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Maybe before we decide who leads, we could list out what we want to pitch? That way, whoever takes it on has a good starting point. Does that sound alright to everyone?

transcript.name: Helena Baxter
transcript.text: Alright, enough circling. We need a decision right now. I have a concrete plan, and unless someone's got something stronger, I'm taking point. Speak up if you disagree, or we're moving.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Helena, your plan might be solid, but if folks aren't on board, it's going to show when we pitch. Maybe we should at least make sure we're all clear on the details before we call it done?

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: If it helps, I think Erik’s right. We should make sure everyone’s clear on what we’re pitching before we pick the lead. I can help list out the main points if that’s useful.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Can we quickly jot down the top three points we want to pitch? Once that’s clear, I’m happy to support whoever steps up, but I think we’ll sound more confident if everyone’s on board with the plan.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Just checking—are we agreed on the three main things we want to pitch, or does anyone want to tweak that list before we settle on who presents?

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Are we missing anything important from that list? Maybe someone wants to add something before we wrap it up? Just making sure we’re not overlooking details.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: I don't have anything to add to the list, but if someone does, now's probably the moment. Otherwise, I think we're ready to decide who takes the lead.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: I think the main points are covered. Anyone here want to speak up about leading before we decide? Otherwise, I’m fine with Helena’s plan if everyone else is.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: If no one else wants to step up, I’m alright with Helena leading. As long as everyone’s comfortable with the plan, I think we should move ahead.

transcript.name: Helena Baxter
transcript.text: Right, I'm taking lead. I expect everyone to back the pitch fully—no side conversations, no last-minute changes. If you've got a real objection, say it now. Otherwise, we're locking this in and getting to work. Agreed?

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: No objections here. Just let me know if you need any numbers double-checked or details filled in. I'll make sure the technical side is squared away.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: Alright, no pushback from me. I’ll double-check our backend integration points so we don’t miss anything technical. If anyone needs specifics, just ping me.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Just to double-check, do we have anyone confirming the client’s latest feedback before we finalize the pitch? I’d rather catch any last-minute changes now than get surprised.

transcript.name: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen
transcript.text: Quick check—has someone already pulled the client’s latest feedback into our draft? Just want to be sure we’re not missing any updates before we finalize.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: If no one has double-checked the client feedback, I can pull it up and confirm we're not missing any last-minute notes. Just let me know.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Alright, sounds like we’re good. Let’s just get that feedback checked, and then I’m set to move on.

transcript.name: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen
transcript.text: If anyone has any last thoughts or concerns—especially if you haven’t spoken up yet—now’s a good time to mention them. Otherwise, I think we’re just about set.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Okay, I’m good with the plan too. If anything does come up, just let me know and I’ll help however I can.

transcript.name: Helena Baxter
transcript.text: Alright, we’re locked. I want first drafts on my desk by noon tomorrow. If you hit a snag, flag it immediately—don’t sit on it. Let’s move.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: Understood. I’ll go through the backend integration pieces later today—if anything looks off, I’ll raise it right away.
